note: Independent source rejudgment after the third-party checker adapter committed in 71b1f3d799, against the unchanged declared partial scope and its current tagged announce, forwarding and interop functions. RFC 2545 Section 3: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Tested: "only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Gap: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if". Producer: internal/component/bgp/reactor/link_scope.go::thirdPartyLinkLocal, with internal/component/bgp/reactor/link_scope.go::linkLocalNextHop. TestRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocalAnnounce sends a next hop naming another router with valid global/link-local neighbor entries on one device and MAC; its common-subnet case requires that router's global followed by fe80::9 with the 32-octet length, and rejects the speaker's fe80::1. Its off-link-recipient case keeps the same usable neighbor view but requires the global-only form. TestRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocalForward drives actual Session receipt and both cached and route-server forwarding rails, varying the third-party global's membership of the recipient's subnet while keeping its neighbor identity known. It requires exactly one announcement with the complete expected MP_REACH value, including unchanged NLRI, so an absent or incorrect pair and a failure to exclude the pair off the common subnet are distinguishable. linkLocalNextHop checks the joint common-prefix condition before thirdPartyLinkLocal, which derives the next-hop entity's link-local through neighborView.linkLocalOf and the same-device/link-layer pairing, never the speaker's configured link-local. The modified checkRFC2545ThirdPartyLinkLocal retains the sink's actual link-local/MAC identity, neighbor-pair precondition, FRR next-hop decode and live-session assertions. Its new native JSON installation check additionally requires the exact selected, installed BGP prefix and that sink link-local as an active FIB next hop in the same entry. FRR vty_show_ip_route and nexthop_json_helper produce those fields. The checker resolves both neighbor addresses before sending and repeats its operator announcement until the known-address case is decoded; that proves no missing-address discovery and no automatic late-entry re-advertisement. The miss paths in thirdPartyLinkLocal still return no address when the table cannot uniquely name the third router, and refreshPeerLinkScopes/refreshForwardFactsIfLiveFrom refresh facts without replaying the route. The declared include-half Gap therefore remains owed and the verdict stays partial, with zero whole-requirement credit. This source judgment does not assert that the pending native green/broken proof pair has completed; proof freshness remains a separate native admission requirement.
